question: Falls in the elderly most commonly have a single identifiable cause such as a trip or slip, and a thorough search for additional contributing factors is usually unnecessary after the immediate cause is identified.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct. Falls in the elderly are multifactorial — always assess intrinsic (postural hypotension, polypharmacy, visual/cognitive impairment, muscle weakness) and extrinsic (environmental) factors even when an apparent single cause exists.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Falls in the elderly are almost always multifactorial. Even when an obvious external cause (trip) is identified, intrinsic risk factors (postural hypotension, visual impairment, polypharmacy, muscle weakness) must be assessed.
